key_facts: July 29 SETTLED UPDATE (Reuters via The Straits Times, July 29/30): Romania's Energy Ministry officially announced on July 29 that Romania will shut down its second (and final) nuclear reactor at Cernavoda early on July 30 due to decades-low Danube river levels (1,650 m3/s on July 28 vs 4,750 m3/s July average; forecast 1,500 m3/s Aug 4), following the shutdown of Unit 1 three days earlier. Nuclearelectrica's two 706-MW reactors at Cernavoda constitute Romania's sole operating nuclear power plant and have never previously been disconnected simultaneously due to low water. Meanwhile Hungary's Paks only shut down 1 of its 4 reactors (partial curtailment, does not qualify). Every resolution criterion (government announcement between July 1 and August 2, 2026 of plans for a complete shutdown of its sole operating nuclear power plant due to drought-related cooling-water shortages) is officially met by Romania. Updated Romania 0.83 -> 0.99.
